subject: Pre-audit evidence request: Art.28/30 extract + DPIA follow-up (NovaBank)
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novabank.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-12T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Pre-audit evidence: Art28/30 ledger excerpt + DPIA follow-up

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the quick intro yesterday. We are opening a small compliance window ahead of our vendor audit in March and I wanted to flag the specific items our privacy team will need so we can confirm scope and timing: 

- A sample Article 30 register extract showing fields you provide to customers (export format, columns and a short row sample).
- The latest DPIA summary / supporting statement for the inference product you will be using (high level controls + identified risks and mitigations).
- Current subprocessors list with onboarding dates and regions of processing.
- Evidence of KMS wrapping / key management for at-rest exports (high-level attestation or sample logs if possible).
- Confirmation of audit access model: do you provide a temporary read-only portal account for auditor access, or curated evidence packages?

I attached our preliminary checklist (nova_pre-audit_checklist.xlsx) to help scope. Can you let me know what you can provide by Jan 20, and whether you need an NDA or auditor PoC from us? Also looping Lisa Grant (privacy) on questions about exports and pseudonymization expectations.

Appreciate it,
Tom

--
Tom Reynolds
Head of Vendor Risk
NovaBank
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novabank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-12T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pre-audit evidence: Art28/30 ledger excerpt + DPIA follow-up

Tom — thanks for the clear checklist and for looping Lisa. We can support all of the items you listed; below is a proposed plan and what we will deliver by Jan 20: 

1) Art.30 sample extract: a CSV with dummy rows and column definitions (redwood-art30-extract-sample.csv). This will show the schema we export for customer processing ledgers.

2) DPIA supporting statement: our product DPIA summary and the 2027 risk/mitigation appendix (redwood-dpia-supporting-statement-2027.pdf). This covers data flows, lawful bases, and mitigations (pseudonymization, retention controls, access controls).

3) Subprocessors: a current inventory export (CSV) with onboarding dates and primary processing regions. We’ll highlight any EU/UK processors and provide the contractual stipulation excerpts for Art.28.

4) KMS attestation: we cannot share raw HSM logs but will provide a KMS wrap statement and a redacted sample of a key-unwrap event trace for audit purposes.

5) Audit access: we offer two options — (A) curated evidence package export (preferred for most customers) or (B) temporary auditor accounts with read-only access and IP-restricted sessions. If you’d like the latter we’ll coordinate SSO & temporary creds. 

Attachments: redwood-art30-extract-sample.csv; redwood-dpia-supporting-statement-2027.pdf.

Next steps: Ben will own delivery of the Art.30 sample and subprocessors extract; Marissa will coordinate the KMS attestation and evidence packaging. Can you confirm whether NovaBank’s auditor needs account access (option B) or if the curated package (option A) is sufficient? If option B, please share auditor name and proposed audit window so we can pre-provision.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novabank.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Lisa Grant <lisa.grant@novabank.com>
Date: 2028-01-12T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pre-audit evidence: Art28/30 ledger excerpt + DPIA follow-up

Neha — perfect, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For the Art.30 extract, could you include a pseudonymized sample (no real identifiers) and an explanation of retention flags so we can spot-check retention controls?
- For KMS: a redacted key-unwrap trace is fine; we will ask for the event IDs so our auditor can reference them during the review.
- Auditor access: Option A (curated package) should be fine for our initial review, but we may request a short read-only session during the week of Feb 20 if anything looks unclear. Please hold that window tentatively.

Also: will you be able to include the subcontractor SCC / DPA excerpt that shows Art.28 obligations and flow-down language? That would save us time in legal review.

Finally, please share a 20–30 minute slot for a short walkthrough next week (Jan 17–19) so our privacy lead can ask a couple of process questions. 

Thanks — Tom
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novabank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-13T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pre-audit evidence: Art28/30 ledger excerpt + DPIA follow-up

Tom — thanks for the clarifications. Confirming action items and owners: 

- Art.30 pseudonymized sample + retention flag doc — owner: Ben Carter — ETA: Jan 19 (attachment: redwood-art30-extract-sample.csv).
- Subprocessor inventory + SCC/DPA excerpt with flow-down clauses — owner: Ben Carter — ETA: Jan 20.
- DPIA supporting statement and product risk appendix — owner: Neha (attached).
- KMS attestation + redacted unwrap event IDs — owner: Marissa Cole — ETA: Jan 20.
- Tentative auditor window (read-only) held for Feb 20–24; we’ll only provision if you confirm.

Let’s do a 25-minute walkthrough on Jan 18 at 10:00am PT — invite sent (calendar link in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-NovaBankAudit). During the session we’ll show the Art.30 export format, retention tagging, and KMS attestation approach. If that works for Lisa and your privacy team we’ll do a short demo and Q&A.

I’m attaching a draft mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-novabank-redwood.docx) which lists the evidence items and timelines — please review and mark any gaps.

If you prefer we can also route the documents through DocuSign for an evidence NDA — let me know.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
